shell.errorReturnDefaultRoot: Could not return to the default project root.

books.intro: Each book has its own tax and currency settings. Use separate books for private and business activity; use separate Kassiber files for different clients.

workspace.empty: No books in this set yet.

create.title: New book
create.descriptionFromSource: Create a separate book in {{workspace}} from {{source}}'s tax settings.
create.descriptionInWorkspace: Create a separate book in {{workspace}} and choose its region and accounting method.
create.descriptionDefault: Create a separate book using default settings.
create.copyHint: Copying settings only copies tax policy, currency, holding period, and lot selection. Wallets, accounts, and transactions stay in the original books.
create.austrianMethodNote: Austrian books use the moving-average method (gleitender Durchschnittspreis) by default. Other methods are available but not standard for Austria.

renameProfile.title: Book settings
renameProfile.description: Rename the book or change its region, accounting method, and supported cost-basis pool scope. Policy changes reprocess journals so reports recompute.
renameProfile.poolScopeNote: Changing the scope invalidates journals so reports can be recomputed.
renameProfile.poolScopeLockedNote: Only the country policy's reviewed global scope is currently available.
renameProfile.austrianMethodNote: Austrian books use the moving-average method (gleitender Durchschnittspreis) by default. Other methods are available but not standard for Austria.

switchRegion.title: Switch region?
switchRegion.body: Change this book from {{from}} to {{to}}, resetting the accounting method to {{method}}.
switchRegion.warning: All journals are reprocessed so reports recompute.

renameWorkspace.title: Edit book set name
renameWorkspace.description: Rename this book set. Books, wallets, and transactions stay unchanged.

createWorkspace.title: New book set
createWorkspace.description: Create a separate top-level set in this local database, then add its first book. Most users only need one.

frame.setupConnects: Setup connects to nothing unless you test a server.

start.headline: Your Bitcoin books, kept on your machine.

openExisting.title: Open existing books
openExisting.tooltipUnavailable: Opening existing books is available in the desktop app

regtest.title: Open Regtest Demo
regtest.body: Skip setup and open the generated regtest book connected to the local Docker stack.

start.quickStartDetail: Built-in Bitcoin servers, local AI, encrypted books, no update checks.

import.title: Open existing books
import.rightBody: The desktop daemon now points at this selected data root. Once a book opens, the same local database powers the rest of the app.
import.empty: No books were found in this local data root.

default.title: Built-in Bitcoin servers
default.description: Explorer API and Electrum / Fulcrum, run by Bitcoin Austria.
default.tradeoff: The operator sees which addresses you look up.

custom.title: Your own server
custom.description: Your own Esplora, Electrum / Fulcrum, Bitcoin Core or Liquid server, over clearnet or Tor.
custom.tradeoff: Only that server sees your addresses.

skip.title: Offline
skip.description: No sync, AI or update checks. Imports and reports still work.

connections.useSslDescription: Most servers use TLS on port 50002.
connections.trustSslDescription: Unsafe. Only for a server you control.
connections.certificateIgnored: Ignored while TLS certificate verification is disabled.
connections.certificateSystemStore: Leave empty to use the system certificate store.
connections.useProxyDescription: Route only this server through Tor, SOCKS or an HTTP proxy.
connections.onionDetectedBody: Uses the local Tor proxy at 127.0.0.1:9050 for this server only.
connections.testHint: Optional — check the endpoint is reachable.
connections.credentialsWarning: Don't paste tokens, passwords or cookies here. Add them after setup.

local.title: Local model
local.description: Ollama, oMLX or another OpenAI Responses-compatible server on this machine.

remote.title: Remote provider
remote.description: An OpenAI Responses-compatible API or a CLI agent (Codex, Claude, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot). Prompts and book context leave this device.

ai.providerPrivacyDescription: TEE providers claim a trusted-execution path. Kassiber still treats them as off-device.
ai.baseUrlDescription: Use an OpenAI Responses API-compatible /v1 endpoint or a supported CLI locator.
ai.remoteAck: I understand prompts may leave this device.
ai.remoteAckDescription: Labels, notes, hostnames and report details can be sensitive.

security.title: Protect your books

plaintext.title: Unencrypted
plaintext.description: Anyone with disk access can read it. For testing only.

security.passphraseNote: Sent only to the local daemon to unlock the database — never stored in the UI.
security.recoveryAck: I understand there is no passphrase recovery path.
security.recoveryAckDescription: If the passphrase is lost, the SQLCipher database cannot be opened.
security.touchIdDescription: Unlock with Touch ID through a Keychain entry. The CLI is enrolled separately.
security.migrateCredentials: Move credentials from backends.env into the encrypted DB.
security.plaintextAck: I understand plaintext mode is not for real wallet data.
security.plaintextAckDescription: Balances, addresses and labels are readable from disk.

sync.title: Choose sync connections
sync.updateChecksDescription: GitHub sees your IP address, Kassiber version and the time.

tax.noteAtCustom: Differs from the Austrian defaults (EUR, moving average).

sync.noteDefaultLoading: Backend addresses are loading from Kassiber.

ai.noteRemote: Receives the book context you approve.

updates.noteEnabled: GitHub sees your IP address, Kassiber version and the time.

storage.noteEncrypted: Passphrase required. Touch ID {{touchId}}. No recovery path.
storage.notePlaintext: Readable by anyone with disk access.

secrets.noteEncrypted: Existing backends.env credentials move into the encrypted database.
